name: Party Management Open API v2
title: Party Management Open API v2
summary: The Party Management Open API v2 provides endpoints for managing parties with a relationship to the enterprise, such as accounts, consumers, and contacts. Use this API to create, update, retrieve, and inactivate records in the Consumer [csm_consumer], Account [customer_account], and Contact [customer_contact] tables.
overview:
The Party Management Open API is a ServiceNow implementation of the TM Forum Party Management API REST specification, based on the TMF632 Party Management API Conformance Profile v5.0.0, June 2025. The API is conformance certified by TM Forum.

This API is provided within the sn_tmf_api namespace. The calling user must have the sn_tmf_api.party_integrator role. The Customer Service Base Entities (com.snc.cs_base) plugin is required.

v2 is the current version of the Party Management Open API and aligns with the TMF632 CTK. Requests use v2 by default. To use a Party Management Open API v1 endpoint, specify v1 in the endpoint path.

You can extend this API to customize required parameters, request body validation, additional REST operations, and field mappings. Sensitive fields, such as phone numbers, may require special ACL permissions for update or retrieval.

members.name: POST /api/sn_tmf_api/v2/party/individual
members.summary: Creates a new individual party management record in the Consumer [csm_consumer] or Contact [customer_contact] tables.
members.html:
URL format

Versioned URL: /api/sn_tmf_api/{version_number}/party/individual

Default URL: /api/sn_tmf_api/v2/party/individual

Supported request parameters

Path parameters
Name Description
api_version Optional. Version of the endpoint to access. For example, v1 or v2. Only specify this value to use an endpoint version other than the latest.

Data type: String
Query parameters
Name Description
None
Request body parameters (XML or JSON)
Name Description
{Request object} Consumer or Contact record to create. Requires @type, givenName, and familyName. A Contact also requires an email entry in contactMedium and an account in relatedParty.
{
  "@type": "String",
  "externalId": "String",
  "name": "String",
  "givenName": "String",
  "middleName": "String",
  "familyName": "String",
  "gender": "String",
  "nationality": "String",
  "title": "String",
  "status": "String",
  "contactMedium": [Array],
  "externalReference": [Array],
  "partyCharacteristic": [Array],
  "relatedParty": [Array]
}
@type Required. Type of individual record to create or update. Replaces the root partyOrPartyRole object from v1. The value isn't case-sensitive.
Valid values:
  • Consumer: Consumer record.
  • Contact: Contact record.

Any other value, including Account, returns an error.

Data type: String
contactMedium List of ways to contact the individual.

For a Contact, a POST request must include an entry with contactType set to email and a valid emailAddress.

Data type: Array of Objects

"contactMedium": [
 {
  "@type": "String",

  "preferred": Boolean,

  "street1": "String",
  "street2": "String",
  "validFor": {Object}
 }
]
contactMedium.@type Schema or subclass type of the contact medium.
Possible values:
  • BusinessPhoneContactMedium: Business phone number.
  • EmailContactMedium: Email address.
  • FaxContactMedium: Fax number.
  • GeographicalAddressContactMedium: Physical address.
  • HomePhoneContactMedium: Home phone number.
  • MobilePhoneContactMedium: Mobile phone number.

Data type: String
contactMedium.city City of the address.

Data type: String
contactMedium.contactType Type of contact channel. Replaces the v1 mediumType parameter.
Possible values:
  • businessPhone: Business phone number.

  • faxPhone: Fax number.
  • homePhone: Home phone number.
  • mobilePhone: Mobile phone number.
  • postalAddress: Physical address.

Data type: String
contactMedium.country Country of the address.

Data type: String
contactMedium.emailAddress Email address. Used when contactType is email.

Data type: String
contactMedium.locationId Sys_id or external_id of an existing location record to link to the individual. Used when contactType is postalAddress.
How the location is handled depends on the record type:
  • Consumer: If you provide a locationId that doesn't exist, the system creates a new location from the address fields and returns a warning. If you omit locationId, the system creates a new location from the address fields.
  • Contact: The locationId must match an existing location. If it doesn't, the address is skipped and the response returns a warning.

members.name: POST /api/sn_tmf_api/v2/party/organization
members.summary: Creates a new party organization record in the Account [customer_account] tables. You can also create and associate Contact and Location records inline during organization creation, eliminating the need for separate POST operations.
members.html:
Automatic Location Creation with contactMedium

When you include address information in the contactMedium field (with @type set to GeographicalAddressContactMedium), the system automatically handles location creation and association based on what you provide:
  1. If you supply a valid locationId, the system links the existing location record to the organization you are creating.
  2. If you provide address attributes (street, city, country, postCode, stateOrProvince) along with an invalid or non-existent locationId, the system automatically creates a new location record with those attributes and associates it to the organization.
  3. If you provide address attributes without specifying a locationId at all, the system creates a new location record and associates it to the organization.
Note:
Location creation requires no mandatory fields. You can provide any combination of address attributes (street1, street2, city, state, postCode, country) based on your needs. If you omit all address attributes from the contactMedium section, no location record is created or linked to the organization.

Inline Contact Creation with relatedParty

When you include contact attributes in the relatedParty field without providing a contact ID, the system automatically creates a new contact record and associates it to the organization you are creating. This eliminates the need for a separate POST request to create the contact first. You can include the following contact information directly in the relatedParty.partyOrPartyRole object.

Mandatory attributes for inline contact creation:
  • familyName
  • contactMedium entry with contactType set to email and a valid emailAddress
Optional attributes:
  • givenName
  • contactMedium entries for businessPhone, homePhone, or mobilePhone

Example: Creating a contact inline without a pre-existing ID.

{
  "relatedParty": [
    {
      "role": "primaryContact",
      "@type": "contact",
      "partyOrPartyRole": {
        "givenName": "John",
        "familyName": "Doe",
        "contactMedium": [
          {
            "contactType": "email",
            "emailAddress": "john.doe@example.com",
            "@type": "EmailContactMedium"
          }
        ],
        "@type": "Individual"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Legacy approach: Linking an existing contact by ID.

If you already have a contact record, you can link it by providing its sys_id instead:
{
  "relatedParty": [
    {
      "role": "primaryContact",
      "@type": "contact",
      "partyOrPartyRole": {
        "id": "existing_contact_sys_id",
        "name": "John Doe",
        "@type": "Individual"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Both approaches are supported. The system automatically determines whether to create a new contact or link an existing one based on whether the partyOrPartyRole includes an id field.
